title: Learning deterministic BPE merges
description: A quick reference for the pair-counting and merge-rule terms used in this chapter.

terms.definition: A tokenization method that repeatedly learns rules for replacing selected adjacent byte-symbol pairs.
An ordered pair of neighboring token IDs that may be selected for the next merge.
The number of adjacent positions carrying one pair, including overlapping positions during selection.
One cycle of counting candidates, choosing a pair, assigning a symbol, and replacing that pair.
The zero-based position of a learned rule in the ordered BPE table, with earlier ranks taking priority.
A fixed rule that chooses the numerically smaller pair when candidate frequencies are equal.
A left-to-right rewrite that consumes each input token at most once.
The exact underlying byte sequence represented by either a raw token or a merged token.
A hard barrier where BPE pair counting stops, preventing pairs from joining separate documents.
